solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rush to have surgery on neck

parts.note: neck and gall both mean cheek or impudence
OP is short for an operation

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hurry along for an operation on their neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' is not the body part but brazen nerve; 'surgery on neck' places the operation after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallop is to move at full speed, as a horse does, so it is a synonym for hurrying.

clue.text: Trouble crossing Peru, oddly, some time in spring

indicators.note: to cross something here is to span it, one word stretching from one side to the other around the second

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

indicators.note: odd means the first, third and fifth positions, so only those letters are kept

parts.note: the odd letters of Peru

explanation.surface: A traveller hits trouble on the way across Peru one spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The trouble word straddles the two odd letters of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: April is a month falling in the northern spring, so it is an example of a period in that season.

clue.text: Socialist mostly concerned with ceremony supporting left

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down answer a word that supports another sits beneath it, so the order is fixed

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
about means on the subject of
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician is preoccupied with pomp and ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the supporting pieces come below, so L tops the answer; ABOUT loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labourite is a supporter of the British Labour Party, which is broadly socialist in tradition.

clue.text: Strait-laced journalist prepared to be fired

parts.note: prim means prudish, strait-laced
ED is short for editor, the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A prudish reporter senses that the sack is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests losing a job, but the definition is about a gun made ready to shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A primed gun or charge has its priming powder in place, so it is ready for discharge.

clue.text: Food rating badly received

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one word takes another inside it

parts.note: a grade is a rating
ill as an adverb means badly

explanation.surface: A restaurant dish is given a poor review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating badly received' reads like a bad review, but the rating word is receiving the word for badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A grillade is a dish of grilled meat, particularly a Creole stew of beef or veal, so it is an example of fare.

clue.text: Swimmer ultimately floundering: where is that wretched rescue vessel?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of floundering

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry state, so these letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A struggling swimmer cries out for a lifeboat that has not arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimmer seems to be the one floundering, but it is the definition; the rescue vessel is a biblical one, not a lifeboat.
explanation.definitionFit: The great white shark is a large predatory fish, so it is an example of a creature that lives in water.

clue.text: I smoke, holding nose to block out oxygen: that's dangerous

indicators.note: to hold is to keep within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to block something out is to exclude it, so that letter goes

parts.note: taken as written, before its O goes
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
to cure fish or meat is to preserve it, as by smoking

explanation.surface: A smoker holds their nose to keep out the oxygen, which is plainly risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' is not tobacco but preserving food over a fire; 'I smoke' is the outer shell holding the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is unsafe or unprotected, so it poses a risk; the sense is close to hazardous.

clue.text: Offal, small portion with top sliced off

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, and slicing it off removes it

parts.note: a sliver is a thin small piece

explanation.surface: A butcher trims a small serving of innards.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIVER loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver is one of the organ meats eaten as offal, so it is an example of that category.

clue.text: Rovers team agreed to recruit players, right?

indicators.note: to recruit is to take people in, so one word enlists another inside it

parts.note: 'done!' means it is agreed
the cast is the players in a production
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A football club manager checks the side has agreed to sign some new players.
explanation.walkthrough: Doncaster Rovers is an English football club; 'team' tells you the place name serves as the club's.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster Rovers is a football club named after its Yorkshire town, so the town name identifies that side.

clue.text: Caught teacher of religion and head showing ill-temper

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A religious teacher and a headmaster are both found to be bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a headteacher but is a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabbiness is grumpy irritability, so it is a synonym for a bad mood or peevish temper.

clue.text: What's very popular with oenophiles, principally?

definitions.text: What's very popular with oenophiles, principally?

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or at the head, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of oenophiles

explanation.surface: A question about what wine lovers like best.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: oenophiles are wine lovers, and the thing they love is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vino is a casual word for wine, and wine is exactly what enthusiastic connoisseurs of the grape enjoy most.

clue.text: Writer's problem with tyre: taxi firm called in

indicators.note: something called in is summoned inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: a flat is a punctured tyre
Uber is the ride-hailing company

explanation.surface: An author with a puncture phones for a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the writer to the wordplay; the taxi firm sits inside the punctured tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustave Flaubert was the French novelist who wrote Madame Bovary, so he is an example of an author.

clue.text: What might have enabled drivers to communicate, seeing road junction?

definitions.text: What might have enabled drivers to communicate
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: a fax machine in a car, for motorists to send messages
second meaning: a place where four roads meet

explanation.surface: Drivers once needed some device to talk to each other at crossroads.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical definition built from two words; the second is a real, rare word, best known as the name of the crossroads at the centre of Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A carfax is an old word for a crossing of four roads, from Old French for four forks.

clue.text: Shop soiled? Not so, the reverse

indicators.note: the reverse of something runs it the other way round, back to front
not here means without, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, and taken away

explanation.surface: A customer asks whether goods are shop-soiled and is told they are not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop soiled' is a phrase for goods marked by handling in a store; here 'shop' breaks off as the definition, and 'Not so' strips two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a store selling cooked meats and fine foods, so it is a kind of retail outlet.

clue.text: Reminiscent of Morse's last case

indicators.note: last means the final one, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of Morse
the vocative is the grammatical case used in addressing someone

explanation.surface: Something recalls Inspector Morse's final investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is a grammatical case, not a detective's; Inspector Morse is the TV detective the surface invokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative brings memories or images to mind, so it is a synonym for suggestive of the past.

clue.text: Woman's not affected by European Union till now

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: affected means altered or disturbed, so these letters change their order

parts.note: EU is the abbreviation for European Union
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman has so far been unaffected by the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not affected' reads as 'unaffected', but 'not' is the fodder and 'affected' its signal; 'by' just places pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereunto is an old legal word meaning up to this point, a synonym for hitherto or thus far.

clue.text: Such eggs a Dutch hen abandoned?

definitions.text: Such eggs a Dutch hen abandoned?

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so these letters run loose

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dutch hen has deserted her clutch.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: eggs a hen abandons are never brooded, so they stay in their shells.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhatched eggs are those whose chicks have not emerged, which is what happens when a sitting bird deserts them.

clue.text: During holiday, Leonard and I head for ancient Spanish city

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one piece falls within the other

parts.note: VAC is short for vacation
Len is a short form of Leonard
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of ancient

explanation.surface: Two holidaymakers head off to an old city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: VAC is short for vacation, and Len is the usual short form of Leonard.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a port city on Spain's east coast founded by the Romans, so it is an example of a large Iberian settlement.

clue.text: Promise man bread with this starter

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or chap
nan is a flat Indian bread

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of this

explanation.surface: A waiter promises a man some bread along with his first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' sounds like the first course of a meal alongside the bread, but it picks out the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a solemn agreement or pledge, so it is a formal synonym for an undertaking.

clue.text: Wild animal centre being spoken of

indicators.note: something spoken of is said out loud, so the word is heard not read

parts.note: the heart is the centre of something

explanation.surface: A wildlife centre is being talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild animal centre' reads as a sanctuary, but the centre word is what is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A hart is an adult male red deer, so it is an example of a creature living in the wild.

clue.text: Suffering setback, boxer facing arrest and jail

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: pug is short for pugilist, a boxer
to nab is to catch or arrest

explanation.surface: A boxer's career takes a knock when he is arrested and locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Bang up is British slang for locking someone in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: To bang up is slang for imprisoning someone, so it is a synonym for locking a person away.

clue.text: Moroccan dish with name in English

parts.note: a tag is a name or label
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A menu gives a North African dish its English name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is not an instruction to insert; it is simply kept as a word between the name and English.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagine is a slow-cooked North African stew named after the conical earthenware pot it is cooked in.

clue.text: Turkish city is on lake, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told reaches us by ear, so the sound counts rather than spelling

parts.note: a mere is a lake, and 'on' places it next to 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a Turkish city lies beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Mere is an old English word for a lake, as in Windermere.
explanation.definitionFit: Izmir is a large port on Turkey's Aegean coast, so it is an example of an urban centre in that country.

clue.text: Start to swot a month before exam — that's most clever

indicators.note: the start of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of swot
MAR is the calendar abbreviation for March
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Beginning revision a month ahead of an exam is the wisest plan.
explanation.walkthrough: To swot is British for studying hard; 'before' simply places the month ahead of the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Smartest is the superlative of smart, meaning brightest or most intelligent of all.

clue.text: Former driver about to leave Riviera town, heading north

indicators.note: in a down answer going north means travelling upwards, from bottom to top
to leave is to go away, so that letter departs

parts.note: Cannes is a resort on the French Riviera
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A retired racing driver is about to drive north out of a Riviera resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to leave' reads as 'on the point of leaving', but 'about' is the letter that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayrton Senna was a Brazilian Formula One world champion who died in 1994, so he is an example of a past racer.

clue.text: Early showings of Falling In Love: mediocre movie

indicators.note: what shows early comes first, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Previews of a romantic film suggest it is no better than average.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showings' and 'movie' pull toward cinema, and indeed the definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Film and movie are British and American words for the same thing, a motion picture.

clue.text: Workman indicted after pinching short length of material

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze between, so one word grips another

parts.note: indicted means formally charged

indicators.note: short means lacking something, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a hank is a coiled length of yarn or thread

explanation.surface: A labourer is prosecuted after stealing a bit of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' looks like stealing but means gripping; HANK loses its K. A chargehand is British for a worker in charge of a small team.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargehand is a worker who leads a gang of others, ranking just below a foreman, so is a type of labourer.

clue.text: We're told much-loved explorer does appear here

indicators.note: what we are told reaches us by ear, so the sound counts rather than spelling

parts.note: dear means much-loved
Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the Niger

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that a beloved explorer really does turn up here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' is not the verb but the plural of doe; only the first half is heard, as the explorer's name is already spelt right.
explanation.definitionFit: A deer park is an enclosed estate stocked with deer, so female deer are what you would see there.

clue.text: Apartment suitable for the family taken by an Italian

parts.note: a pad is informal for a flat
U, for universal, is the British film certificate for all ages
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family-friendly flat is rented by an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An Italian' looks whole, but 'an' is wordplay and only 'Italian' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A Paduan is a native of Padua, a city in northern Italy, so is an example of an Italian person.
